title: Operator approval strobe — prototype notes
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes for the "Operator Approval Strobe" concept — a lightweight, event-driven approval gate that reduces audit payload size and approval latency for customer-managed networking changes. Target audience: product, SRE, infra, and security reviewers. This doc is intentionally informal: sketch, experiments, sample traces, and a rollout checklist.

Summary of idea

- Problem: full-fidelity audit bundles for every VPC/edge change create high retention cost, slow approval UX, and lengthy evidence review cycles. Customers want strong attestation and traceability but not a heavy data bill or slow handoffs.
- Hypothesis: we can get 95% of forensic value with a strobe approach — emit dense proof packets on a short time-window boundary plus sparse sampled detail for a small fraction of changes. This preserves deterministic, cryptographic checkpoints while drastically reducing per-change payload.
- Goal: create a developer-facing approval primitive (API + operator CLI + minimal UI) that establishes an "approval window" and produces a compact proof token that can be replayed to a forensic system.

Key concepts (glossary)

- Approval Strobe: a short-lived time boundary (e.g., 10s to 2m) where compact, signed change receipts are aggregated into a canonical proof.
- Compact proof token: base64-encoded signed blob with change summary, minimal telemetry, and a merkle root reference to sampled evidence.
- Evidence shard: detailed logs/packets pushed to customer-owned storage or to our encrypted escrow for a sampled subset.
- Sample budget: per-customer monthly allowance (number of full-evidence captures) with burst allowances for incident/replay.

Acceptance criteria (initial)

- Attestation: every approval returns a compact proof token signed by Redwood operator key with timestamp and sequence id.
- Traceability: for any compact proof token, we can expand to a human-readable change summary within 30s and full sampled evidence retrieval within 3 minutes when evidence is available.
- Cost: median per-change stored payload reduced >= 75% vs current change-evidence bundle baseline.
- Latency: approval round-trip (UI->approve->token) < 1.2x current fastest approval, and interactive UI should not block longer than 5s for commits that only return compact tokens.

Operational flow (example)

1) Operator initiates a change via operator UI/CLI or via API: POST /v1/customer/{cid}/change with payload describing intent (route add, firewall update, peering claim) and an operator signature.
2) System assigns change to current strobe window (e.g., window-2025-02-03T10:15:00Z/00:00:30).
3) Each participant (customer operator, Redwood agent) contributes a tiny transcript entry (hash of the config delta, actor id, nonce).
4) At window close, the service computes a merkle root of transcripts and signs it — producing compact proof token (token includes root, window id, short human summary).
5) Token returned to operator and stored in change index; if this change is drawn for sampling, we also persist full evidence (packet captures, syslog, gcps) to escrow.

Sampling policy (proposal)

- Deterministic baseline: sample 1 in N changes (N configurable per customer) by hashing change fingerprint together with a monotonically increasing sequence and thresholding. Deterministic sampling ensures reproducible test corpora.
- Risk-based augmentation: increase sampling probability for high-risk changes (CIDR changes, route deletions, operator-attestation-lifted flags).
- Ad-hoc forensic capture: allow customers to request a retrospective capture for a short window (within retention TTL) — consumes sample budget and triggers live evidence harvest.

API contract (sketch)

- POST /v1/private/{cid}/changes (body: {intent, operator_id, risk_flags}) -> 202 Accepted, {token, window, eta_full_evidence_if_sampled}
- GET /v1/private/{cid}/change/{id}/proof -> 200 {compact_token, verification_signature, summary}
- POST /v1/private/{cid}/request-evidence -> 202 {request_id, budget_consumed}

UX notes

- In console, show a small badge: "Compact proof ready" with a link to expand summary. For sampled changes show "Detailed evidence available — click to retrieve" and a warning that retrieval may take up to 3 minutes.
- For operator CLI, add `rw approval strobe submit --intent=...` which returns short proof token and a retrieval flag. Add `rw approval strobe fetch-evidence --id=...` to pull full evidence.

Runbook and incident scenarios

- Rollout: start internal-only for 2 weeks, then opt-in customers (security-conscious but cost-aware) for 4–6 weeks, then wide default for new accounts.
- Incident: if a sampled evidence retrieval fails, escalate to SRE on-call and trigger emergency capture (temporary override of sample budget). Capture logs: agent-heartbeat, operator-signatures, network traces.
- Reconstitution: when full evidence is restored, replay merkle root verification locally to ensure principal alignment.

Telemetry and KPIs

- Ratio compact_vs_full: percent of changes that returned compact-only tokens vs full evidence.
- Sample-hit-latency: time from request to evidence availability (goal median < 180s).
- Proof-verify-rate: fraction of compact tokens successfully verified by internal verifier on first attempt (> 99.9%).
- Cost-saved: aggregate data storage reduction in GB/month relative to baseline.

Security and trust model

- Keys: Redwood signs compact tokens with operator signing key stored in HSM. Customer may optionally request customer-managed key signing (KMK) mode where the same token is additionally signed by customer KMS.
- Tamper-resistance: merkle root anchors to a per-window chaining ledger; window anchors rotated and checkpointed to an immutable append-only store.
- Legal: compact tokens are short summaries and do not contain PII; detailed evidence stored in customer-owned S3/GCS when possible. Default retention for sampled evidence is 90 days unless elected otherwise.

Open questions / TODOs

- Window sizing: what is the right default (30s vs 120s) across workloads? Need perf experiments with 50/100/500 RPS change workloads.
- Sampling budget UX: a per-customer quota is required; what are sensible defaults for small business vs enterprise? How to surface burst allowances?
- Forensic fidelity: what minimum set of fields in compact token are necessary to make triage meaningful? (actor_id, change_hash, window_id, risk_flags, minimal telemetry)
- Regulatory constraints: EU customers may require full-evidence retention in-region; ensure evidence shard placement options.

Experiment plan (short)

- Metric: validate that monthly storage per-customer falls by >= 60% after enabling strobe for non-sampled changes.
- A/B: internal rollout to 50% of test accounts with strobe vs baseline for one month. Track incident triage time and SLO impacts.
- Perf: synthetic test that simulates 200 ops/s across 10k customers to measure strobe window compute and signature latency.

Notes to reviewers

- This is intentionally a lightweight draft. Focus feedback on: (1) operational safety (e.g., emergency capture mechanics), (2) UX clarity for sample retrieval, (3) legal/regional data placement limitations.
- Links above point to a Linear ticket and a prototyping PR. If we proceed, I'll draft a more formal PRD with data model, auth contract, and detailed security review.

Quick sketches / example tokens (toy examples)

- Compact token (humanized): {window: "2025-02-03T10:15:00Z/30s", root: "ab4f...", summary: "route-add 10.0.0.0/16 <- peer-888", signed_by: "redwood-op-v2"}
- Evidence retrieval flow (CLI): rw approval strobe fetch-evidence --token ab4f... -> returns pre-signed URL to escrow bucket or triggers customer-push.

Appendix: ops checklist for first 2-week internal pilot

- Prepare HSM signing key + rotation policy (ops)
- Implement deterministic sampling toggle and default N=100 (engineering)
- Console: badge + sample retrieval CTA + small explainer (DX)
- CLI: submit/fetch commands + short help text (DX/engineering)
- Telemetry hooks: compact_vs_full, proof-verify-rate, sample-hit-latency (observability)
- Security review: threat model, retention policy, legal opt-ins for region (security/legal)

-----

Rough signoff: Aisha (owner), Marco (eng lead), Evelyn (product), Priya (security).

Notes to self: keep this doc as the lightweight experiment log; if we converge, migrate content into PRD: approval-strobe-prd-v1.
